column7: I am a PhD professor. I have read Giving Voice to Values by Mary C. Gentile, and I have also listened to the audio version. I teach this class, so I thought that instead of rereading (or listening to) the material each time, I'd find a reliable summary source to review and jog my memory. When I viewed the content on this site for the book, I found it overly superficial for my needs. For example, Gentile gives 12 assumptions. The summary mentions that there are 12 but only gives one. There is no depth or even a simple listing of the 12 assumptions. Because I teach various classes, I was looking for a way to save some time and not have to reread the material for each class all the time. Based on what I've seen in the Gentile summary, I would be better off with my current note-taking system and rereading. I will also admit that I have not reviewed any other books on this site, so other summaries may be more sufficient for my needs. However, I don't want to explore more books and then risk not being eligible for a refund, so I kindly ask that my full amount for the year subscription is returned to my credit card. Thank you.
